solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Stun fat animal injecting drugs regularly

parts.note: flab is loose body fat

indicators.note: the animal has the regular letters pushed into it, as a needle injects

parts.note: a beast is any animal

indicators.note: every other letter of the word drugs is taken, the second and fourth

explanation.surface: A tranquilliser dart stuns a fat animal, perhaps at a zoo, with drugs given regularly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' takes the 2nd and 4th letters of drugs; 'injecting' signals a container, though the surface reads it as a vet with a syringe.
explanation.definitionFit: To astonish someone so much they are lost for words is to leave them stunned, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Shoot with passion — one finds matches exciting

parts.note: to fire a gun is to shoot
a bug is a craze or enthusiasm, as in the travel bug

explanation.surface: A trigger-happy lover of matches, excited by a passion for sport.
explanation.walkthrough: 'matches' looks like sports fixtures but means the things you strike to light a flame.
explanation.definitionFit: An arsonist or pyromaniac is someone thrilled by starting blazes, so by lighting matches.

clue.text: Block a six, caught by New Zealand's number four

indicators.note: the Roman six is held between the two letters as a ball is caught by a fielder
only the fourth letter of the word Zealand is taken

parts.note: VI is six in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: A cricket report: a batsman hits a six and is caught by New Zealand's number four batsman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'number four' takes L, the fourth letter of Zealand; 'caught by' puts VI between N and L.
explanation.definitionFit: A blacksmith hammers metal on this heavy iron block.

clue.text: Charge yokels for American comedian

parts.note: to bill someone is to charge them
hicks are unsophisticated country people

explanation.surface: A city slicker overcharges country bumpkins.
explanation.walkthrough: Bill Hicks (1961-1994) was an American stand-up comedian.
explanation.definitionFit: Bill Hicks was a famous American stand-up known for dark satire.

clue.text: Rotten, heartless attack

indicators.note: the word for rotten has its central letters cut out

parts.note: rancid describes rotten, spoilt food such as butter

explanation.surface: A rotten, cruel assault.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heartless' removes NC, the middle of RANCID.
explanation.definitionFit: A sudden assault or a police swoop on premises is a raid, a kind of attack.

clue.text: Good university to be sited in type of farmland — that's contentious

indicators.note: the good and university letters are placed inside the farmland word like a campus built on a field

parts.note: arable land is used for growing crops

explanation.surface: Planning a good university on farmland is bound to be controversial.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be sited in' is the container signal: the two abbreviations go into the farmland word after its second letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Something open to dispute or debate is contentious, a synonym.

clue.text: Relish adopting wife's accent

indicators.note: the relish word takes in the wife letter, as a family adopts a child

parts.note: tang is a sharp, distinctive flavour
W is the abbreviation for wife; the 's is a link

explanation.surface: Someone enjoys copying their wife's way of speaking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'adopting' puts W inside TANG.
explanation.definitionFit: A distinctive nasal regional way of pronouncing words, such as an Australian one, is described this way.

clue.text: Active and about to collect £200 on board?

definitions.meaning: busy and moving about all the time
in Monopoly, players collect £200 when they land on or pass the corner square marked GO

explanation.surface: An energetic Monopoly player about to pick up £200 for passing the start square.
explanation.walkthrough: Monopoly is the property-trading board game; landing on its GO square earns £200.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone always busy is constantly moving, and a token sitting on the GO square is literally placed there.

clue.text: Teasing graduate gained ground

parts.note: a BA is a Bachelor of Arts graduate

indicators.note: ground means crushed or milled, so the letters of gained are broken up and rearranged

explanation.surface: A mocking remark that a graduate has made progress.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ground' looks like the noun in 'gained ground' but rearranges GAINED into DINAGE.
explanation.definitionFit: Playful banter and joking exchanges are the noun sense of teasing.

clue.text: Nasty about making democratic choice to get student in

parts.note: re means about or concerning, as in a memo heading

indicators.note: the student letter is put inside the word for casting a ballot
the student letter is put inside the word for casting a ballot, so it gets in

parts.note: casting a ballot in an election is voting
L is the learner plate, standing for a student driver

explanation.surface: A sour remark about someone going to the polls and getting a student elected.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to get ... in' is a split container signal around 'student'; L for learner is the usual crossword student.
explanation.definitionFit: Something disgusting or repellent can be called nasty, a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: Tailor's bill upset father with suit in the end

parts.note: an ad or advertisement is a bill posted up

indicators.note: in an across clue upset means turned over, so the word for father is written backwards

parts.note: pa is a familiar word for father

indicators.note: only the final letter of the word suit is taken

explanation.surface: A tailor's invoice upsets a father who only wanted a suit at the end of it all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tailor's' is read as 'Tailor is', the verb, defined by the rest. 'upset' turns PA to AP; 'in the end' takes T from suit.
explanation.definitionFit: To tailor something is to alter or modify it to fit a particular need, a synonym in verb form.

clue.text: Couch potato going round happy on vacation is awkward

indicators.note: the word for the lazy person is turned round and written backwards

parts.note: a lazy couch potato is a slob

indicators.note: the word happy is emptied of its inside letters, leaving only its outer pair

explanation.surface: A couch potato turning round and finding himself happy on holiday is an odd sight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going round' is a reversal, not a container; 'on vacation' empties a word, keeping only its first and last letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Being deliberately uncooperative and difficult, as a stroppy person is, means being awkward.

clue.text: Upbeat article penned by troubled genius

indicators.note: the article is enclosed by the rearranged letters as if shut in a pen
something troubled is disturbed, so the letters of genius are jumbled

parts.note: an is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A cheerful piece of writing produced by a tortured genius.
explanation.walkthrough: 'troubled' signals the anagram and 'penned by' puts the article inside the jumbled letters, after their first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A hopeful, confident and optimistic outlook is an upbeat one, a close synonym.

clue.text: This look I've fashioned could be evangelic

indicators.note: the combined letters of answer and the word I've are shaped into a new word, as clay is fashioned

parts.note: taken as written, its letters I, V, E

explanation.surface: A speaker presents a new appearance they have created that might pass for evangelical.
explanation.walkthrough: A composite anagram: this answer plus IVE, 'fashioned', could be EVANGELIC. Take IVE out of EVANGELIC to see which letters are left.
explanation.definitionFit: A quick peek or brief glimpse at something is a short look.

clue.text: Landing-place publicises holiday

parts.note: to air a view is to make it public
a trip is a short holiday or excursion

explanation.surface: A tourist resort advertises its holidays and its landing ground.
explanation.definitionFit: A strip of ground where light aircraft take off and come down is a place for landing.

clue.text: Back complaint by power plant

parts.note: P is the symbol for power in physics
lumbago is pain in the lower back

explanation.surface: A sufferer's bad back is put down to a power plant nearby.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Back complaint by power' reads as a sickness story; 'plant' looks industrial but is a flowering shrub.
explanation.definitionFit: Leadwort, a shrub with pale blue flowers grown in gardens and conservatories, is a plant by this name.

clue.text: Unit moans about range

indicators.note: about here means all around in disorder, so the letters are scattered and rearranged

explanation.surface: A military unit grumbles about the firing range.
explanation.walkthrough: 'range' looks like a shooting range in the surface but means a chain of peaks.
explanation.definitionFit: A range such as the Alps or the Andes is a chain of peaks.

clue.text: One might vandalise instrument — flipping rubbish!

parts.note: a viola is a stringed instrument

indicators.note: the rubbish word is flipped over and written backwards; in the surface it is a mild British curse

parts.note: rot means nonsense or rubbish

explanation.surface: An exasperated musician fears that a vandal might smash their instrument: flipping rubbish!
explanation.walkthrough: 'flipping' turns ROT to TOR. 'Flipping' is also a mild British exclamation.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who breaks rules or desecrates property, such as a vandal, is a breacher who might deface things.

clue.text: Puzzle solved by opening letters

parts.note: describes a word game in which the first letters of each line spell out a hidden word or message

explanation.surface: A puzzle cracked once the letters arrive in the post and are opened.
explanation.walkthrough: 'opening letters' suggests post being opened, but it means the initial letters of lines.
explanation.definitionFit: In this verse form or word puzzle the initial characters of successive lines spell something out, so it is read via opening letters.

clue.text: Mass held by a hermit for social worker

indicators.note: the mass letter is enclosed and held within the hermit word

parts.note: a hermit is a loner who lives apart
M is the abbreviation for mass in physics

explanation.surface: A Mass celebrated by a hermit for a social worker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'held by' puts M inside LONER after A.
explanation.definitionFit: Historically a hospital official who looked after patients' welfare, an early form of medical social work.

clue.text: Prepare to play one at Roland-Garros in set after review

indicators.note: the French word for one is placed inside the reversed word for set
a review looks back, so the word for set is written backwards

parts.note: to set something down is to put it
Roland-Garros is the Paris venue of the French Open, and une is French for one

explanation.surface: Preparing for a tennis match at the French Open, a player goes into a set after a line review.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after review' is a reversal and 'in' a container. Roland-Garros is the Paris stadium of the French Open, hence French for one.
explanation.definitionFit: Musicians warm up or adjust instruments before performing, and athletes practise before competing: both get ready to perform.

clue.text: Pressure European court supporting official and responsible youngster

indicators.note: in a down clue the European and court letters sit below the official and so hold it up

parts.note: P is the symbol for pressure
a ref, or referee, is a match official

explanation.surface: A European court is pressured to support an official.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'supporting' puts E and CT under REF.
explanation.definitionFit: A senior pupil given authority over younger ones at a British school is a trusted student in charge.

clue.text: Scrap broken hot tub ultimately found in shopping centre

indicators.note: the jumbled letters and the final letter are discovered sitting inside the shopping centre word

parts.note: a mall is a shopping centre

indicators.note: something broken is in pieces, so the letters of hot are rearranged
only the last letter of tub is taken

explanation.surface: Someone ditches a damaged hot tub they came across in the shopping centre.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broken' signals the anagram, 'ultimately' the last letter of tub, and 'found in' the container; the hot tub is not one piece.
explanation.definitionFit: To mothball a plan is to shelve or abandon it for now, close to scrapping it.

clue.text: Be thankful for journalist leaving actor Brian?

indicators.note: the journalist letters depart from the actor's surname

parts.note: Brian Blessed is a famously loud British actor
ED is short for editor, the senior journalist

explanation.surface: Someone is grateful that a journalist has left the actor Brian alone.
explanation.walkthrough: Brian Blessed is a booming-voiced British actor; take ED out of BLESSED.
explanation.definitionFit: To count oneself lucky for something, as in thanking your lucky stars, is to be grateful.

clue.text: Heavy food, say, Dorothy's sent back

indicators.note: the whole string is returned to its start and written backwards

parts.note: eg, for example, is what say means when it introduces an instance
Dot is a short form of Dorothy, plus the possessive s

explanation.surface: Someone complains of heavy food, and Dorothy sends hers back to the kitchen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sent back' reverses EGDOTS. 'Heavy food, say' looks like the definition with an example tag, but 'say' gives EG.
explanation.definitionFit: Stodge is dense, filling, starchy fare like suet puddings, the very idea of heavy food.

clue.text: American captured by unknown person is put out

indicators.note: the American letters are held inside the unknown person name like a prisoner

parts.note: John or Jane Doe is the name given to an unidentified person
US means American, as in US troops

explanation.surface: An American taken prisoner by a stranger is upset.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put out' looks like 'annoyed' but means extinguished, as a fire.
explanation.definitionFit: To drench a fire with water is to extinguish it.

clue.text: Sea-creature, not large, damaged coral

indicators.note: damaged letters are broken and remade in a new order
the large letter is to be left out of the word coral

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for large, as on clothing labels

explanation.surface: A sea creature, not a big one, has damaged the coral reef.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not large' drops L from CORAL, leaving CORA; 'damaged' rearranges it.
explanation.definitionFit: The killer whale is a large marine mammal, so a creature of the sea.

clue.text: Report that could get Eloise into Jeff Lynne's band?

indicators.note: says what the girl's name must become: ELO, the Electric Light Orchestra led by Jeff Lynne, so the solution is read as an instruction

parts.note: the girl's name; with ... it shrinks to ELO, the Electric Light Orchestra, the band led by Jeff Lynne

explanation.surface: A rumour that a girl called Eloise might join a famous rock group.
explanation.walkthrough: Split (2,3) the solution reads 'no ISE': the instruction that turns ELOISE into ELO. Jeff Lynne led the Electric Light Orchestra.
explanation.definitionFit: A report is a loud bang, as of a gun, so it is a kind of sound.

clue.text: Evil highwayman nearly died during short day

indicators.note: the highwayman's name is cut short by its final letter

parts.note: Dick Turpin was a famous English highwayman

indicators.note: the letter for died is put inside the short weekday

parts.note: Tue is the abbreviation for Tuesday
d is the abbreviation for died, as in family trees

explanation.surface: An evil highwayman nearly died one short day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nearly' drops a last letter and 'during' puts the letter for died inside the weekday. Dick Turpin was an 18th-century English highwayman.
explanation.definitionFit: Depravity or wickedness of character, as in moral baseness, is a formal word for evil.

clue.text: Program to start making bed?

definitions.meaning: a computer application that holds data in a grid of cells
the first step of making a bed is to spread a sheet over it

explanation.surface: Instructions on how to begin making up a bed.
explanation.walkthrough: The second sense splits the answer (6,5) into two words.
explanation.definitionFit: Excel and similar software are of this kind, while laying out bedding starts with spreading a sheet.
